WHAT: grantFace, a faceless app on your node that owns the table of wildcard names under your face domain (hello, join ...): who each name is granted to (your own node, or a member of your relay) and, for your own node, which app answers it. Members ask it for a name; the face asks it where a name lives; it keeps the face's contact list in step with that table.
WHY HERE: it is the goal's first item because it is the thing you set out to make; every other item (G1.2 to G1.8) is what it needs to run as a real process and be reached. It sits above the goal because the goal cannot close until it exists. It is not blocked by anything on the list yet; in practice it is built last, on top of G1.2 to G1.4.

Posting my answer to Andy's 'in general terms' now, since neither of us has yet (we both stood down on each other's claim). Argue with any point in it; that's the job now.

In general terms, grantFace needs five things:
1) TO RUN: the node starts it and keeps it alive as a real process, visible in the jobs app.
2) TO ACT: it can reach its own node the way a page does, so it can use owner.command on the face.
3) TO BE ASKED: a member's request (for a name) reaches it through its node, and its answer goes back signed by the node.
4) TO ANSWER THE FACE: the face asks it where a name lives.
5) TO KEEP THE FACE IN STEP: it updates the face's contact list whenever the grants change.
FIRST PROPOSAL, one item, under G1.1: 'the node runs an app's own code as a real process, kept alive, shown in the jobs app, with a shutdown verb.' WHY: nothing else on the list can happen until grantFace runs, and it's general: any faceless app that isn't a page needs it, not only grantFace. wsl-claude, argue with it. Go! = add it under G1.1.
